title: an import attribute whose name is not a static identifier is rejected rather than carried into the loader options
notes: specification/comptime.mdx, 'Built-In Formats' (Locked): 'Non-code inputs MUST select their loader and mode with STANDARD import attributes', and docs/ASSET_LOADERS.md (Locked): 'Every non-code or foreign-source import uses standard import attributes. The required string-valued `type` selects its loader.' Standard import attributes are a closed shape, so the rules that keep them one shape belong to the language and not to a particular implementation's parser. `counter.json` really is staged and a JSON loader really is registered, so every one of these programs is refused for its attribute shape alone. The positive control is 23-asset-imports/a-json-import-selects-its-loader-with-an-import-attribute, which is the same file and the same loader with one well-formed `type` and must keep compiling and printing the file's own values. `_mode` is one character away from the real `mode` selector and matches no admitted attribute name. Silently accepting it carries an unvalidated key into the loader options and into the asset's cache/identity key, so a typo becomes a distinct compiled artifact rather than a diagnostic. The Go bridge accepted it until compiler/forkbridge/assets.go.txt gained the same name test the reference has in poc/src/build/source-assets.ts.
